--- ## 📖 Table of Contents - [What is AUGMENTIX-AI?](#-what-is-augmentix-ai) - [Why AUGMENTIX-AI?](#-why-augmentix-ai) - [Key Features](#-key-features) - [Technical Innovation](#-technical-innovation) - [Quick Start](#-quick-start) - [Architecture](#-architecture) - [Core Concepts](#-core-concepts) - [Real-World Examples](#-real-world-examples) - [Advanced Usage](#-advanced-usage) - [API Reference](#-api-reference) - [Performance & Benchmarks](#-performance--benchmarks) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [Citation](#-citation) --- ## 🎯 What is AUGMENTIX-AI? AUGMENTIX-AI is a **production-grade, research-inspired platform** that transforms tabular data augmentation from an art into a science. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on random noise or naive duplication, AUGMENTIX-AI combines: - 🔬 **Statistical Rigor** - Mathematical foundations, not guesswork - 🤖 **AI Intelligence** - LangGraph multi-agent reasoning - ✅ **Quality Assurance** - Comprehensive validation pipeline - 🔒 **Constraint Enforcement** - Business rules guaranteed - 📊 **Model Awareness** - Performance-driven generation - 💡 **Full Transparency** - Every decision explained ### **The Problem We Solve** Traditional data augmentation is broken: - ❌ Random noise destroys correlations - ❌ SMOTE alone ignores constraints - ❌ No validation of augmented quality - ❌ Black-box processes - ❌ No understanding of "why" augmentation helps ### **Our Solution** AUGMENTIX-AI is a **complete ML infrastructure** that: - ✅ Preserves statistical properties - ✅ Enforces domain constraints - ✅ Validates every augmentation - ✅ Explains all decisions - ✅ Improves model performance measurably ### **Core Philosophy** > *"Statistical methods for data generation. AI agents for reasoning. Never confuse the two."* 1. **All numeric data is generated using pure mathematics** (scipy, numpy) 2. **LLaMA agents reason about strategy, constraints, and safety** (LangGraph) 3. **Every augmentation is validated through multiple statistical tests** 4. **Complete transparency with comprehensive logging and explanations** --- ## 🌟 Why AUGMENTIX-AI? ### **The Data Augmentation Landscape** | Approach | Statistical Rigor | AI Reasoning | Validation | Constraints | Explainability | Production Ready | |----------|-------------------|--------------|------------|-------------|----------------|------------------| | **Random Noise** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | **Basic SMOTE** | ⚠️ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ⚠️ | | **GANs/VAEs** | ⚠️ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | **AUGMENTIX-AI** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ### **What Makes Us Different** #### 1️⃣ **Statistical Foundation** We don't guess. Every augmentation is grounded in probability theory: - **Kernel Density Estimation** for smooth distribution sampling - **Gaussian Copulas** for preserving complex correlations - **Bootstrap Methods** for variance-preserving resampling - **Multivariate Normal** for correlated feature generation #### 2️⃣ **AI-Powered Intelligence** Six specialized LangGraph agents reason about your data: - 🔍 **Schema Semantic Analyzer** - Understands column meanings - ⚖️ **Constraint Generator** - Proposes business rules - 🎯 **Policy Reasoner** - Determines optimal strategy - 🛡️ **Safety Reviewer** - Validates quality and safety - 💬 **Augmentation Explainer** - Generates human narratives - 🗣️ **NL Config Interpreter** - Parses natural language commands #### 3️⃣ **Multi-Layered Validation** Every augmented dataset passes through: - **Distribution Tests** (Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Chi-square, Wasserstein) - **Drift Detection** (PSI, Mean/Std shifts, Correlation changes) - **Constraint Verification** (Business rule compliance) - **Performance Validation** (ML model improvement) - **Safety Review** (AI-powered quality assessment) #### 4️⃣ **Production Architecture** Built for real-world deployment: - Modular, testable codebase (10 independent modules) - Type-safe Python with comprehensive error handling - Professional Streamlit UI with 7 interactive pages - Complete logging and audit trails - Configurable via YAML or natural language - Export-ready results with detailed reports --- ## ✨ Key Features ### 🔬 **Intelligent Augmentation** ### 🔬 **Intelligent Augmentation**
🔢 Numeric Feature Augmentation **Method 1: Gaussian Noise Injection** ```python X_augmented = X_original + N(0, intensity × σ) ``` - Preserves mean and variance - Configurable intensity (0.0 - 0.5) - Respects feature ranges **Method 2: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE)** ```python kde = KernelDensity(kernel='gaussian', bandwidth=optimal) X_augmented = kde.sample(n_samples) ``` - Non-parametric distribution modeling - Captures complex, multimodal distributions - No assumptions about underlying distribution **Method 3: Bootstrap Resampling** ```python X_augmented = resample(X_original, n_samples, replace=True) ``` - Variance-preserving - Ideal for small datasets - Statistical guarantees **Method 4: Correlated Feature Generation** ```python Σ = cov(X) # Covariance matrix X_augmented ~ N(μ, Σ) ``` - Preserves inter-feature correlations - Multivariate normal sampling - Maintains feature dependencies
🏷️ Categorical Feature Augmentation **Method 1: Probabilistic Sampling** ```python P(category) = observed_frequency / total_count X_augmented ~ Categorical(P) ``` **Method 2: Conditional Sampling** ```python P(category | other_features) from empirical distribution ``` - Respects category co-occurrence patterns - Maintains realistic combinations **Method 3: Balanced Sampling** ```python Oversample rare categories to match target distribution ```
⚖️ Class Imbalance Handling **SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique)** ```python x_new = x_i + λ × (x_nn - x_i) where x_nn is k-nearest neighbor ``` - Generates synthetic minority samples - Interpolates between existing samples - Configurable k-neighbors (default: 5) **ADASYN (Adaptive Synthetic Sampling)** ```python Density-based sample generation ``` - Focuses on harder-to-learn minority regions - Adaptive sample distribution **Target Ratio Control** ```python minority_samples / majority_samples = target_ratio ``` - Configurable (0.5 - 1.0) - Automatic minority class detection
🎨 Synthetic Data Generation **Gaussian Copula Method** ```python 1. Transform features to uniform marginals: U = F(X) 2. Fit Gaussian copula: Z = Φ⁻¹(U) 3. Sample from Gaussian: Z_new ~ N(μ, Σ) 4. Transform back: X_new = F⁻¹(Φ(Z_new)) ``` - Preserves marginal distributions - Captures complex dependencies - Handles mixed data types
### 🤖 **LangGraph Multi-Agent System**
```mermaid graph TD A[Input Data] --> B[Schema Semantic Analyzer] B --> C[Constraint Generator] C --> D[Policy Reasoner] D --> E[Statistical Augmentation] E --> F[Safety Reviewer] F --> G[Augmentation Explainer] G --> H[Validated Output] style B fill:#667eea style C fill:#764ba2 style D fill:#f093fb style E fill:#4facfe style F fill:#43e97b style G fill:#fa709a ```
🔍 Agent 1: Schema Semantic Analyzer **Purpose**: Understand the meaning and role of each column **Capabilities**: - Identifies semantic types (ID, PII, amount, rate, count, categorical) - Detects potential data leakage (e.g., target-correlated IDs) - Groups related features (demographics, financial, behavioral) - Flags high-cardinality columns **Output Example**: ```json { "customer_id": { "semantic_type": "identifier", "recommendation": "exclude_from_augmentation", "reason": "Unique identifier, not predictive" }, "credit_score": { "semantic_type": "risk_metric", "recommendation": "preserve_distribution", "reason": "Critical for model, has specific range [300-850]" } } ```
⚖️ Agent 2: Constraint Generator **Purpose**: Propose business rules and logical constraints **Constraint Types**: 1. **Range Constraints**: `18 ≤ age ≤ 100` 2. **Ratio Constraints**: `loan_amount ≤ 0.5 × income` 3. **Logical Constraints**: `if premium_customer then credit_score ≥ 700` 4. **Dependency Constraints**: `years_employed ≤ age - 18` **Example Output**: ```python { "constraints": [ { "type": "range", "column": "age", "min": 18, "max": 100, "confidence": 0.95 }, { "type": "ratio", "numerator": "loan_amount", "denominator": "income", "max_ratio": 0.5, "rationale": "Standard debt-to-income ratio" } ] } ```
🎯 Agent 3: Policy Reasoner **Purpose**: Determine optimal augmentation strategy **Decision Factors**: - Dataset size (small/medium/large) - Class imbalance ratio - Feature types distribution - Task type (classification/regression) - Model type (if provided) **Strategy Levels**: ```python aggressive_augmentation: intensity=0.3, ratio=0.9 # Heavy imbalance moderate_augmentation: intensity=0.2, ratio=0.8 # Medium imbalance light_augmentation: intensity=0.1, ratio=0.7 # Balanced data conservative_augmentation: intensity=0.05, ratio=0.6 # Large dataset ``` **Output Example**: ```json { "strategy": "moderate_augmentation", "intensity": 0.2, "target_ratio": 0.8, "focus_areas": ["minority_class", "boundary_regions"], "rationale": "Class imbalance of 0.3 detected. Moderate SMOTE + noise recommended." } ```
🛡️ Agent 4: Safety Reviewer **Purpose**: Final quality and safety assessment **Review Checklist**: - ✅ Distribution drift within acceptable limits (PSI < 0.2) - ✅ All constraints satisfied (100% compliance) - ✅ Statistical tests passed (p-value > 0.05) - ✅ Model performance improved or maintained - ✅ No data leakage introduced **Verdict Options**: 1. **SAFE**: All checks passed, proceed confidently 2. **WARNING**: Minor issues, review recommended 3. **REJECT**: Significant problems, do not use **Example**: ```json { "verdict": "WARNING", "message": "Minor drift in 2 features, but performance improved by 3%", "issues": [ { "severity": "minor", "feature": "employment_years", "psi": 0.15, "threshold": 0.2 } ], "recommendation": "Acceptable for use. Monitor in production." } ```
💬 Agent 5: Augmentation Explainer **Purpose**: Generate human-readable explanations **Explanation Components**: 1. **What was done**: "Generated 50 samples using SMOTE + KDE" 2. **Why it was done**: "To balance minority class and improve model recall" 3. **How it was validated**: "Passed KS-test (p=0.42), PSI=0.08" 4. **Expected impact**: "Estimated 5-10% improvement in F1-score" **Output Format**: Markdown narrative report
🗣️ Agent 6: NL Config Interpreter **Purpose**: Parse natural language configuration **Examples**: ```python "Balance the dataset but keep it conservative" → strategy='conservative', balance_classes=True, intensity=0.05 "Generate 100 samples focusing on high-risk customers" → n_samples=100, filter='risk_score > 0.7', method='smote' "Don't touch age or income, they're sensitive" → protected_columns=['age', 'income'] ```
### ✅ **Comprehensive Validation**
📊 Distribution Testing **1. Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test** (Numeric Features) ```python D = max|F_original(x) - F_augmented(x)| p-value from KS statistic ``` - Tests if two distributions are identical - Threshold: p-value > 0.05 (95% confidence) **2. Chi-Square Test** (Categorical Features) ```python χ² = Σ((O - E)² / E) ``` - Compares observed vs expected frequencies - Threshold: p-value > 0.05 **3. Wasserstein Distance** (Earth Mover's Distance) ```python W(P, Q) = min E[‖X - Y‖] ``` - Measures distribution similarity - Threshold: < 0.1 (normalized)
🌊 Drift Detection **1. Population Stability Index (PSI)** ```python PSI = Σ((actual% - expected%) × ln(actual% / expected%)) ``` - PSI < 0.1: No significant drift - 0.1 ≤ PSI < 0.2: Moderate drift - PSI ≥ 0.2: Significant drift (reject) **2. Mean/Std Drift** ```python drift_mean = |μ_aug - μ_orig| / μ_orig drift_std = |σ_aug - σ_orig| / σ_orig ``` - Threshold: < 10% change **3. Correlation Drift** ```python Δρ = |corr_matrix_aug - corr_matrix_orig| ``` - Ensures feature relationships preserved
🏆 Performance Validation **Cross-Validation Comparison**: ```python scores_original = cross_val_score(model, X_orig, y_orig, cv=5) scores_augmented = cross_val_score(model, X_aug, y_aug, cv=5) improvement = mean(scores_augmented) - mean(scores_original) ``` **Metrics**: - **Classification**: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC - **Regression**: RMSE, MAE, R², MAPE **Requirements**: - No significant performance degradation - Ideally: 2-5% improvement
### 🔒 **Constraint System** ### 🔒 **Constraint System**
AST-Based Rule Engine **Safe Expression Evaluation**: - No `eval()` or `exec()` - uses Python's AST module - Type-checked at parse time - Prevents code injection attacks **Supported Rules**: 1. **Range Rules**: ```python engine.add_range_rule('age', min_value=18, max_value=100) engine.add_range_rule('credit_score', min_value=300, max_value=850) ``` 2. **Ratio Rules**: ```python engine.add_ratio_rule('loan_amount', 'annual_income', max_ratio=0.5) # Ensures: loan_amount / annual_income ≤ 0.5 ``` 3. **Expression Rules**: ```python engine.add_expression_rule("age >= 18 and age <= 100") engine.add_expression_rule("credit_score > 600 if premium_customer else credit_score > 500") ``` 4. **Dependency Rules**: ```python engine.add_dependency_rule("years_at_company <= age - 18") ``` **Automatic Filtering**: ```python violations = validator.validate(augmented_df) clean_df = validator.filter_valid_data(augmented_df) # Only constraint-satisfying rows retained ```

--- ## 🚀 Quick Start ### **Installation** (2 minutes) ```bash # Clone or download the project cd augmentix_ai # Install dependencies pip install -r requirements.txt # (Optional) Configure LLaMA # Edit config.yaml and set llama.enabled: true ``` ### **Option 1: Quick Start Script** ⚡ ```bash python quick_start.py ``` **What it does**: 1. Loads sample financial dataset (10 customers) 2. Profiles data automatically 3. Generates augmented samples with SMOTE 4. Validates quality (distribution tests, drift, constraints) 5. Exports to `augmented_output.csv` 6. Prints comprehensive report **Expected Output**: ``` ================================================================================ AUGMENTIX-AI - Quick Start Example ================================================================================ 📤 Step 1: Loading sample data... ✅ Loaded 10 rows, 9 columns 🔍 Step 3: Profiling data... ✅ Profiling complete Strategy: moderate_augmentation Intensity: 0.20 🚀 Step 4: Augmenting data... ✅ Augmentation complete Original: 10 samples Augmented: 15 samples (+5) ✅ Step 5: Validating quality... 🎯 Safety Verdict: SAFE Distribution Tests: ✅ PASSED Drift Detection: ✅ NO DRIFT 💾 Step 7: Exporting results... ✅ Exported to: augmented_output.csv ``` ### **Option 2: Streamlit UI** 🖥️ ```bash streamlit run ui/streamlit_app.py ``` Then open http://localhost:8501 in your browser. **Interactive workflow**: 1. Upload your CSV 2. Review auto-detected schema 3. Configure augmentation settings 4. Click "Run Augmentation" 5. Review validation results 6. Download augmented data ### **Option 3: Python API** 🐍 ```python from pipeline import AugmentixPipeline import pandas as pd # Load your data df = pd.read_csv("your_data.csv") # Initialize pipeline pipeline = AugmentixPipeline(random_state=42) # Analyze data (auto-detect schema, fit distributions, find correlations) analysis = pipeline.fit( df, target_column='your_target', task_type='classification' # or 'regression' ) # View LLaMA-generated policy print(f"Strategy: {analysis['policy']['strategy']}") print(f"Rationale: {analysis['policy']['rationale']}") # Augment with recommended settings augmented_df = pipeline.augment( balance_classes=True, # Only for classification # Or specify custom parameters: # n_samples=100, # intensity=0.15, # methods=['kde', 'smote'] ) print(f"Generated {len(augmented_df)} samples from {len(df)}") # Validate quality validation = pipeline.validate() print(f"Safety Verdict: {validation['safety_verdict']['verdict']}") print(f"Message: {validation['safety_verdict']['message']}") # Check individual metrics if validation['distribution_tests']['all_passed']: print("✅ All distribution tests passed") if not validation['drift_detection']['has_significant_drift']: print("✅ No significant drift detected") # Generate comprehensive report report = pipeline.generate_report() print(report) # Export if safe if validation['safety_verdict']['verdict'] in ['SAFE', 'WARNING']: pipeline.export_data("augmented_output.csv") print("✅ Exported augmented data") else: print("⚠️ Review validation results before using augmented data") ``` --- ## 🏗️ Architecture ### **System Overview**
